lines.text: Sannu. [Hello.] Card number? Sit, they'll call you.
Visiting? Two at a time, please. Two.
Good morning. You're here for a visit or a check? Either way, sit.
You're welcome. Rest. That's your only assignment today.
Sannu fa. [Take heart.] You'll be better soon.
Light gone! Generator, please, now is your moment!
Torches on. Nobody touch the drips. Calm, calm.
Light's back. Everybody breathe.
Number forty-two! Forty-two! …Has anybody seen forty-two?
The queue is for everybody. Even the impatient.
Bring your card, your folder and your patience. Mostly patience.
His mother brought food for the whole ward. Nobody is complaining.
Visitors, lower your voices, please. People are healing.
Sleep under your net, eh? It's not decoration.
Drink water. Eat proper food. Garri alone is not a diet.
He says he's fine. He's here, so sit down, Mr. Fine.
The lab results will be ready by four. Hospital four.
Wash your hands. Yes, again. Hands forget.
Who brought the flask of pap? The whole bench is smelling it. Bless you.
She's asleep now. Go and eat something. Then come back.
Night shift. That bench by the ward is warm again. It always is.
Shh. Everybody's sleeping. Even the generator is whispering.
The statue in the garden faces this way at night. Funny, eh?
Blackout again. We stitched a hand by phone torch yesterday.
Students come in tired, not sick. Eat, sleep, come back.
The mall has three generators. We have one. A brave one.
They cut our line again. Somebody is selling our light.
Strike. The students who stayed come here to talk. We listen.
Free clinic today. Bring anybody who's been sitting too still.
Whatever happens outside, the night nurses are here.
I can't confirm what's in any video. Confidentiality. Sit.
Medicine Week stall: free blood pressure, free advice, free smiles.
An old patient came back to say thank you. Five years later. Made my week.
Our house officers are graduating. Who will we shout at now?
Freshers' medical! Line here, forms there, stop panicking.
Exam week. No sleep, headaches. Water, food, bed. Not more coffee.
Results day. One fainted, one danced. Both are fine. Sit.
Strike or not, this ward stays open.
Football injury? Sit. Ice. The match is over. Let it go.
Election week. Sore throats from shouting. Honey and warm water.
Convocation. Our nurses' children are graduating. The ward is smiling.
Fasting and dizzy? Break gently. Water and dates first.
Christmas on the ward. The patients chose the colour of the lights.
Visitors with flowers. Patients pretending not to be pleased.
Harmattan. Dry eyes, cracked lips, coughs. Drink water. Cover up.
